transcript:
Header: Recorded 2026-08-19 14:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Marcus Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SA); Evelyn Hart (Crimson Head of Security), Samir Patel (Crimson DevOps), Rita Gomez (CTO), Liam O'Connor (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): Discussed critical/ high findings from recent red-team / pen test, agreed remediation owners and patch windows, KMS migration plan, and next steps for re-test.

00:00 Marcus Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Marcus from Redwood, i think we have the full list here, uh, i'll hand off to priya to run through the pen-test highlights and sev breakdown?
00:18 Priya Shah: Yeah hi, thanks. So we got the report yesterday from NorthBridge security, right — they ran the red-team in late July. I'll go through highest sev first. There's one kubelet privilege escalation (CVE-2026-1234) that they've flagged as critical because of node-level access. There's also an auth bypass on an older internal admin endpoint in the payments service, that one's high. We have a few med/low items — cookie flags, CSP headers, dependency vuln - mostly third-party libs.
00:48 Evelyn Hart: Mm-hmm, ok. That kubelet callout is the one Samir's been worried about. Samir, are you seeing evidence of that in prod?
00:55 Samir Patel: Uh, we saw some noisy logs last week but we haven't confirmed exploit, the patch's been out from upstream but we haven't pushed it fleet-wide. We're on a weekly patch window on Tuesdays but there's been hesitation about rebooting worker nodes because of performance windows.
01:10 Marcus Nguyen: Right, so discussion point: emergency hotfix process versus regular cadence. For critical items we recommend immediate patch + canary + quick rollback plan. Priya, do we have a suggested playbook?
01:22 Priya Shah: Yeah, we prototype a 3-step: apply to staging, run smoke tests, then canary 5% of traffic for two hours, monitor KV cache and tail latency. For node level CVEs we also recommend cordon+drain with pod disruption budgets. We'll share an ops snippet.
01:40 Rita Gomez: Does Redwood provide any automation for patch rollouts if we use Dedicated or Private? That could save Ops time.
01:47 Omar Reyes: On Dedicated we have an ops automation library customers can opt into — it's not fully managed patching but there are Terraform modules and runbooks. For Private deployments we can collaborate on an automated job you own, or we can offer a managed run if you take an Enterprise support bundle.
02:05 Liam O'Connor: Quick compliance question: what is the default audit log retention and format? The pen-test called out gaps in a few logs for our EU tenants.
02:15 Priya Shah: Default is 90 days for standard hosted, but you can configure longer retention for Dedicated/Private. We can export logs in JSONL or Parquet into your S3/GCS, and we keep schema samples in the docs. We'll send an example query.
02:30 Evelyn Hart: We need EU-only storage for some projects due to contract clauses. Can you confirm region pinning for logs and keys?
02:37 Omar Reyes: Yes, region pinning is available in Private and Dedicated — we can provision a region-specific logging stack and KMS key. For hosted, we have EU regions but won't do customer-managed keys by default.
02:48 Samir Patel: That KMS point - we were hoping to own key material (BYOK) for some datasets. Is Redwood able to support BYOK / HSM import?
02:57 Priya Shah: Short answer: yes. We support external KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure BYOK) and HSM-based key wrapping for Private. There's a small integration checklist: key policies, rotation windows, and service principal perms. We'll share a Terraform snippet.
03:15 Marcus Nguyen: Ok good. Let's talk secure SDLC. The pen-test mentioned outdated dependencies in the payments microservice. Do you use a centralized dependency scanning tool?
03:25 Evelyn Hart: We've got Snyk for most repos but some internal services are on an older pipeline. The recommended change was to add pre-commit scanning and fail builds on critical vulns.
03:33 Priya Shah: That's standard — we push sbom generation into CI, run dependency scans, and gate merges on severity thresholds. Redwood's recommended policy is fail CI on critical and add a 72-hour mitigation SLA for high.
03:47 Samir Patel: 72 hours is aggressive for high in our schedule, but maybe doable with on-call rotation. What does Redwood require for acceptance after a patch? Do you want evidence?
03:57 Marcus Nguyen: We typically require a remediation note, PR link, and staging verification steps. For SOC 2/ISO evidence we ask for the ticket and verification steps to be kept in the audit trail.
04:10 Rita Gomez: Speaking of SOC2, where are we in that process? We asked earlier about Redwood's SOC2 Type II window.
04:18 Omar Reyes: Redwood's most recent Type II report is Q2 2026; we can share a redacted copy and a controls matrix. We'll attach it to the follow-up email. ISO 27001 is in progress, certification expected by Q1 2027.
04:31 Liam O'Connor: We'll need the controls matrix to map to our internal evidence requirements.
04:34 Omar Reyes: Yep we'll include mapping notes.
04:38 [00:04:45 approx - casual cross talk] Someone: mm-hmm / okay / right

05:00 Priya Shah: Back to technicals — the pen test also flagged RBAC misconfig on an internal dashboard where role propagation wasn't honoring groups. Looks like the AuthN layer had a stale mapping from our old Okta connector.
05:14 Evelyn Hart: Yeah that dashboard's not public but it should only be accessible to SREs. We recently moved to Okta SCIM but sync wasn't propagating a couple groups.
05:22 Samir Patel: We saw group mapping lag of about 20 minutes when a user was deprovisioned; that was the window the tester used. Okta push sync vs SCIM check — we need to harden group removal flows.
05:34 Priya Shah: With SSO, best practice is enforce deny-by-default at the app layer and rely on SAML assertion group claims plus periodic reconciliation. We can help with a sample SCIM config that shortens sync intervals.
05:46 Marcus Nguyen: Also enabling session revocation on deprovision is important — we can suggest SAML session hooks or token TTL tuning.
06:00 Evelyn Hart: Good. On auditability — the report said a missing correlation id in some REST calls made forensic traceability harder. Can Redwood add request-id propagation in client SDKs?
06:12 Priya Shah: We already have a request-id header in our SDKs, but if your services don't propagate it we'll show a patch to set and forward it from the gateway. We'll add examples for Node/Python.
06:25 Samir Patel: That will help triage.

06:40 Rita Gomez: Is there anything about network segmentation? The red-team mentioned lateral access from a dev box to a staging DB.
06:46 Priya Shah: For that we recommended strict network policies and host-level firewalls; for Private we can support NSGs and customer-controlled subnets. For hosted we separate customer traffic at the tenant layer and use strict egress rules.
07:00 Evelyn Hart: Ok. Let's capture remediation priorities — what should be P0/P1?
07:05 Priya Shah: P0: kubelet CVE-2026-1234 (node-level), auth bypass on payments. P1: RBAC mismatch and session revocation windows. P2: deps and headers. P3: docs/hardening notes.
07:18 Marcus Nguyen: We'll annotate the report with those labels and send an aggregated spreadsheet.
07:22 Samir Patel: Sounds good. About the KMS handoff — we need to test wrap/unwarp during rotation to ensure no downtime. How does Redwood recommend rotation?
07:32 Omar Reyes: Recommended pattern: key rotation with key aliasing + double write during rollovers, and you must test unwrap in staging. For BYOK we do a key import flow and then rotate with a cross-check window. We'll share a runbook.
07:45 Priya Shah: Also keep in mind token TTLs for long-running inference caches — if KV cache keys expire, sessions might fail; we recommend a grace period and a live canary on rotation.
07:58 Marcus Nguyen: There's a short debate sometimes about telemetry vs PII in logs. The pen-test flagged an instance where stack traces with small PII leaked into logs.
08:08 Evelyn Hart: Yes that was our mistake — debug=on in prod for a short window. We fixed it but need an automated sensor to flip debug flags in emergencies only.
08:18 Priya Shah: We suggest a feature-flag gating for debug that requires SSO approval to enable, and log scrubbing for known patterns.

08:35 [08:35 - 20:00 mostly detailed technical Q&A, timestamp excerpts]
12:02 Samir Patel: Quick question on log exports: if we push to customer S3, can we auto-invalidate old logs to satisfy GDPR right-to-be-forgotten requests?
12:12 Omar Reyes: Yes you can set lifecycle policies. For audit traces we advise keeping an indexed tamper-evident store for compliance while storing binary artifacts elsewhere. We'll propose an architecture note.

18:40 Priya Shah: On the secure SDLC side, we talked about SBOMs — generate and store them per build and attach to releases. That will make verification simpler for SOC audits.
18:55 Rita Gomez: We also need a CVE response runner — a lightweight internal playbook to triage and classify.
19:05 Marcus Nguyen: Redwood has a template for that and we'll drop it in the follow-up.

24:30 Evelyn Hart: About the re-test, what are acceptance criteria? If the pen-test failed a check due to missing header we fixed, what is your acceptance bar?
24:40 Priya Shah: Acceptance is 'no exploitable path present' for critical and high — we list test steps and for critical we prefer a re-test showing exploit attempt fails or is patched with evidence. Ideally vendor re-scan and a short verification doc.
24:56 Samir Patel: Ok we can commit to that; we'll try to have re-test by early September.

30:10 Marcus Nguyen: Anything else on encryption — customer-managed keys, rotation frequency? Typical requirement is 90-180 days rotation for symmetric keys?
30:20 Omar Reyes: We recommend 90 days for data-at-rest CMEKs in regulated environments, but many customers run annual rotation with additional envelope key rotation. For HSM-backed keys rotation is policy-driven.
30:34 Liam O'Connor: Can we get a matrix mapping controls to rotation cadence recommended for SOC2?
30:38 Omar Reyes: Yes will include in docs.

36:00 [Small tangent about dedicated vs hosted pricing and latency/cost tradeoffs; not fully transcribed]

41:12 Priya Shah: I'll capture the SCIM snippet: reduce sync interval to 1 minute and add immediate deprovision hook. That will address the 20-minute window the tester exploited.
41:25 Samir Patel: Ok we'll apply in staging first.
41:30 Evelyn Hart: Also, can Redwood redact PII in shared screenshots in reports? NorthBridge included some user emails in logs.
41:38 Marcus Nguyen: Yes we'll provide redacted copies for audits.

48:00 Omar Reyes: To summarize: Redwood to share SOC2 artifact, KMS integration checklist, Terraform snippet for automation, and runbook templates. Crimson to patch critical CVEs, enable SCIM quick sync, and prepare staging evidence for re-test.
48:20 Marcus Nguyen: Next cadence — runbook review 2026-08-28, re-test week of 2026-09-07. Priya will send the follow-up with attachments.

55:10 Rita Gomez: One last item — if we go Private for some EU workloads, what's the uplift for support and patch SLAs?
55:20 Omar Reyes: Private has an enterprise uplift, we can include a patch SLA addendum and a managed patching option in the quote. We'll include options in the follow-up.
55:35 Evelyn Hart: Thanks, appreciate it.
55:40 Marcus Nguyen: Thank you all. We'll send notes and artifacts.
55:45 [Call ends]
